/* ---- the guard ---------------------------------------------------------------- */
static void blocked(const char *what, uint32_t ip){
    char b[16];
    g_st.blocked++;
    if (g_st.blocked <= 20 || g_st.blocked % 1000 == 0)
        roam_log("[roam] BLOCKED %s %s (test harness: loopback only; %llu refused so far)\n",
                 what, roam_ip_str(ip, b), (unsigned long long)g_st.blocked);
}
int roam_plat_guard(int test_mode, uint32_t ip, int is_bcast){
    if (!test_mode) return 1;
    if (is_bcast){ blocked("broadcast to", ip); return 0; }
    if ((ip >> 24) != 127){ blocked("sendto", ip); return 0; }
    return 1;
}

/* ---- sending (with the lock held, from either thread) ------------------------------ */
static uint16_t be16(uint16_t v){ return (uint16_t)(v >> 8 | v << 8); }
static uint32_t be32(uint32_t v){ return v >> 24 | (v >> 8 & 0xFF00u) | (v << 8 & 0xFF0000u) | v << 24; }
static void do_send(uint32_t ip, uint16_t port, const uint8_t *buf, int len, int is_bcast){
    if (!roam_plat_guard(g_cfg.test_mode, ip, is_bcast) || g_fd == INVALID_SOCKET) return;
    struct sockaddr_in sa; memset(&sa, 0, sizeof sa);
    sa.sin_family = AF_INET; sa.sin_port = be16(port); sa.sin_addr.s_addr = be32(ip);
    int n = sendto(g_fd, (const char *)buf, len, 0, (struct sockaddr *)&sa, sizeof sa);
    if (n == len){ g_st.sent++; g_st.sent_bytes += (uint64_t)len; return; }
    g_st.send_err++;
    if (g_st.send_err <= 5 || g_st.send_err % 1000 == 0){
        char b[16];
        int e = WSAGetLastError();
        roam_log("[roam] sendto %s:%u failed: Winsock error %d%s\n", roam_ip_str(ip, b), port, e,
                 e == WSAEACCES ? " (broadcast not allowed on this socket)" :
                 e == WSAENETUNREACH || e == WSAEHOSTUNREACH ? " (no route: is the PC on the same network?)" :
                 e == WSAEWOULDBLOCK ? " (send buffer full)" : "");
    }
}
static void io_send(void *u, uint32_t ip, uint16_t port, const uint8_t *buf, int len){ (void)u; do_send(ip, port, buf, len, 0); }

int roam_bcast_targets(const roam_if *ifs, int n, uint32_t *out, int max){
    int k = 0;
    if (k < max) out[k++] = 0xFFFFFFFFu;
    for (int i = 0; i < n && k < max; i++){
        const roam_if *f = &ifs[i];
        if (!f->up || f->loopback || !f->can_broadcast || !f->mask || f->mask == 0xFFFFFFFFu) continue;
        if (!rc_addr_private(f->addr)) continue;            /* only private LANs */
        uint32_t b = (f->addr & f->mask) | ~f->mask;
        int dup = 0; for (int j = 0; j < k; j++) if (out[j] == b) dup = 1;
        if (!dup) out[k++] = b;
    }
    return k;
}
static void io_broadcast(void *u, uint16_t port, const uint8_t *buf, int len){
    (void)u;
    if (g_cfg.test_mode || !g_cfg.discovery){ roam_plat_guard(1, 0xFFFFFFFFu, 1); return; }
    roam_if ifs[32]; int n = 0;
    INTERFACE_INFO il[32]; DWORD got = 0;
    if (WSAIoctl(g_fd, SIO_GET_INTERFACE_LIST, 0, 0, il, sizeof il, &got, 0, 0) == 0){
        int m = (int)(got / sizeof il[0]);
        for (int i = 0; i < m && n < 32; i++){
            if (il[i].iiAddress.Address.sa_family != AF_INET) continue;
            roam_if *f = &ifs[n++];
            memset(f, 0, sizeof *f);
            snprintf(f->name, sizeof f->name, "if%d", i);
            f->addr = be32(il[i].iiAddress.AddressIn.sin_addr.s_addr);
            f->mask = be32(il[i].iiNetmask.AddressIn.sin_addr.s_addr);
            f->up = !!(il[i].iiFlags & IFF_UP);
            f->loopback = !!(il[i].iiFlags & IFF_LOOPBACK);
            f->can_broadcast = !!(il[i].iiFlags & IFF_BROADCAST);
        }
    }
    uint32_t t[16]; int k = roam_bcast_targets(ifs, n, t, 16);
    for (int i = 0; i < k; i++) do_send(t[i], port, buf, len, 1);
}
static void io_event(void *u, int ev, int peer, const char *text){ (void)u; roam_game_event(ev, peer, text); }

/* ---- receiving and the timers (network thread, or the frame hook) ---------------------- */
static void pump(void){
    uint8_t buf[1500];
    int64_t now = roam_plat_now_us();
    for (int k = 0; k < 256; k++){
        struct sockaddr_in sa; int sl = sizeof sa;
        int n = recvfrom(g_fd, (char *)buf, sizeof buf, 0, (struct sockaddr *)&sa, &sl);
        if (n < 0){
            int e = WSAGetLastError();
            if (e == WSAECONNRESET || e == WSAEMSGSIZE) continue;  /* an ICMP for an earlier datagram; an oversized one */
            break;                                                   /* WSAEWOULDBLOCK: nothing more */
        }
        if (sa.sin_family != AF_INET) continue;
        uint32_t ip = be32(sa.sin_addr.s_addr); uint16_t port = be16(sa.sin_port);
        roam_plat_lock();
        g_st.recv++; g_st.recv_bytes += (uint64_t)n;
        if (n > RC_MAX_DGRAM){ g_s->rx++; g_s->rx_bad++; }
        else rc_receive(g_s, ip, port, buf, n, now);
        roam_plat_unlock();
    }
    if (now >= g_next_tick){ roam_plat_lock(); rc_tick(g_s, now); roam_plat_unlock(); g_next_tick = now + 10000; }
}
static DWORD WINAPI net_main(LPVOID u){
    (void)u;
    uint32_t mx = roam_win_mxcsr_default();            /* the core's floats: round to nearest, no FTZ/DAZ */
    __asm__ volatile ("ldmxcsr %0" :: "m"(mx));
    while (!g_stop){
        fd_set rs; FD_ZERO(&rs); FD_SET(g_fd, &rs);
        struct timeval tv = { 0, 5000 };
        (void)select(0, &rs, 0, 0, &tv);
        pump();
    }
    return 0;
}
/* NetThread=0: called by the frame hook instead */
void roam_win_poll(void){ if (g_fd != INVALID_SOCKET && !g_threaded && g_s) pump(); }

int roam_plat_start(const roam_plat_cfg *cfg, rc_session *s){

    roam_plat_lock(); s->io = io; roam_plat_unlock();
    g_stop = 0; g_next_tick = 0;
    const char *nt = roam_opt("NFSU2_ROAM_NETTHREAD");
    g_threaded = !(nt && nt[0] == '0' && !nt[1]);
    if (g_threaded){
        g_thr = CreateThread(0, 64 * 1024, net_main, 0, 0, 0);
        if (!g_thr){ roam_log("[roam] CreateThread failed (%lu): polling from the game's frames instead\n", GetLastError()); g_threaded = 0; }
    }
    roam_log("[roam] UDP %s:%u open%s%s\n", g_cfg.test_mode ? "127.0.0.1" : "0.0.0.0", g_cfg.port,
             g_cfg.test_mode ? " (test harness: loopback only)" : g_cfg.discovery ? ", LAN discovery on" : "",
             g_threaded ? "" : ", polled from the frame hook");
    return 0;
}
/* exiting: whether the network thread may still hold the lock (at process
 * exit Windows has already stopped every other thread) */
void roam_plat_stop(uint8_t reason){
    if (g_fd == INVALID_SOCKET) return;
    mu_init();
    if (TryEnterCriticalSection(&g_mu)){ rc_shutdown(g_s, reason); LeaveCriticalSection(&g_mu); }
    g_stop = 1;
    if (g_thr){ WaitForSingleObject(g_thr, 200); CloseHandle(g_thr); g_thr = 0; }
    closesocket(g_fd); g_fd = INVALID_SOCKET;
}

/* after a fault inside the frame step: the game thread may hold the
 * session lock (any depth); let it go, or the network thread waits forever */
void roam_plat_fault_unlock(void){
    if (g_mu_init != 2) return;
    for (int i = 0; i < 64 && g_mu.OwningThread == (HANDLE)(uintptr_t)GetCurrentThreadId(); i++) LeaveCriticalSection(&g_mu);
}
/* 1 when nobody else holds the session lock (process exit: then nobody can) */
int roam_plat_quiesced(void){
    if (g_mu_init != 2) return 1;
    if (!TryEnterCriticalSection(&g_mu)) return 0;
    LeaveCriticalSection(&g_mu);
    return 1;
}

/* "a.b.c.d[:port], ..." without sscanf; IPv4 literals only (no DNS) */
static int num(const char **p, unsigned *v, unsigned max){
    const char *q = *p; unsigned x = 0; int nd = 0;
    while (*q >= '0' && *q <= '9' && nd < 6){ x = x * 10u + (unsigned)(*q - '0'); q++; nd++; }
    if (!nd || x > max) return 0;
    *v = x; *p = q; return 1;
}
int roam_plat_parse_peers(const char *list, int test_mode, uint16_t defport, uint32_t *ip, uint16_t *port, int max){
    int n = 0;
    if (!list) return 0;
    const char *p = list;
    while (*p && n < max){
        while (*p == ' ' || *p == ',' || *p == ';' || *p == '\t') p++;
        if (!*p) break;
        char tok[64]; int k = 0;
        while (*p && *p != ',' && *p != ';' && *p != ' ' && *p != '\t' && k < 63) tok[k++] = *p++;
        tok[k] = 0;
        const char *t = tok; unsigned a, b, c, d, pt = defport;
        int good = num(&t, &a, 255) && *t++ == '.' && num(&t, &b, 255) && *t++ == '.' && num(&t, &c, 255) && *t++ == '.' &&
                   num(&t, &d, 255);
        if (good && *t == ':'){ t++; good = num(&t, &pt, 65535) && pt != 0; }
        if (!good || *t){
            roam_log("[roam] peer \"%s\" ignored: write a.b.c.d or a.b.c.d:port (IPv4 numbers, no names)\n", tok);
            continue;
        }
        uint32_t v = a << 24 | b << 16 | c << 8 | d;
        if (test_mode && a != 127){ roam_log("[roam] peer %s REFUSED: test harness, only 127.x.x.x peers\n", tok); continue; }
        ip[n] = v; port[n] = (uint16_t)pt; n++;
    }
    return n;
}

# Changelog

## 0.42.6 — direct worker loading and scoped 60946132 support

Adds the exact reviewed game build **60946132**. Its scoped native port covers the existing AI bridge, pace/corner hooks, rails, Drag handoff/protection, owned skill and paired catch-up. Online still requires the separate explicit permission. Stop, manual takeover, stale ownership and permission withdrawal retain their native guards.

The production page now supplies a verified compiled module through its existing game-worker startup observer. It leaves WebAssembly.compileStreaming unchanged. Per-worker message order, immediate port transfers, original shared-memory identity and primary/secondary worker consistency are checked offline. A timed-out, unsupported or failed preparation retains the original game module with tools disabled. Memory-port startup stays unverified and has no page memory tools.

The replacement is authorized by freshly read build metadata, an import/export interface check and complete source/output hashes. An opaque original compiled module cannot be hashed through this interface; matching its import/export names is an eligibility check, not proof of its bytes. Only the independently compiled replacement receives a verified tool profile.

On 60946132, **the tuner, leased forward geometry, per-target corner feedback, online car-category controls, race capture and destination travel are unavailable** pending their separate ports. Their implementations and previous build profiles remain included. The full 102c8d92 pipeline retains its exact prior output.

Current game guards, monitoring and report serialization are retained. A positive encoder result means serialization succeeded, including for reports containing observations. The offline checks do not establish multiplayer acceptance, account status or measured driving results.

The offline report check reproduced a selected-car-state observation from the actual NOS refill: one changed frame and observation flag 16 in controlled race and free-roam monitor contexts. Untouched baselines had zero changed frames and zero flags. The observed fields survived local encoding; no report was sent. This uses bounded native fixtures and synthetic session state, not a full game run. A different loader does not establish a report-free refill route.

The exact captured page check returned zero marks through updated startup and four fixture ticks; the frozen 0.42.5 startup produced API-wrapper mark 2. The fixture uses native-callable browser stand-ins, clean settings and default tool selections. Worker instance postMessage remains wrapped and is not selected by that captured check. Report markers and configuration remain unchanged. These page results do not cancel the separate native NOS observation.

## 0.42.0 — game build 102c8d92, and "Stay on rails" for cleaner corners

- New game build: nfsu2.xyz now serves build 102c8d92. 0.41.0 did not recognise it, so the native AI driver would not load. 0.42.0 adds an exact profile for it (module SHA-256 2ba0b075…, 38,867,137 bytes).
- How the port was made: the reviewed ed8d3359 hook set (bridge, pace, corner and braking targets, walls and car contacts, Drag, Drift, nitrous, forward preview, route choice, catch-up, paired pace, skill 9) was replayed onto the new build as one pinned transform, `native-transplant-102c.js`. Every changed function keeps all of the new build's own instructions in order; only authored instructions are inserted, with function, type and host-address references moved to the new build's values. Input and output are pinned by SHA-256 (output f113eb5d…, 39,052,721 bytes) and the result must pass WebAssembly validation, or nothing is changed.
- Rails: the game drives opponents on a simplified physics mode and flips a car to full physics after a contact. Your racer record made that flip permanent for your AI-driven car, which is where the wall hits at raised pace came from. **Stay on rails** (Race / outrun tuning, on by default) keeps your race AI car on the simplified mode in solo Circuit, Sprint, URL and Street X. It is a guard in Car::SetPhysicsMode that only acts for the car the extension's AI owns, in a solo road race, while the page asks for it.

The paired power/grip boost is not used on rails because it is far too strong on simplified physics. Drag keeps the paired boost. Turning rails off restores the 0.41.0 behaviour.
- Stuck watchdog: if the car stays under 2 m/s for 3 seconds the rails release so normal physics can recover it, and return after 2 seconds above 20 m/s. At most two releases per race.

- Offline checks: the shipped transform reproduces the tested module byte for byte and rejects a wrong hash, changed bytes, the old build and an already patched module; the rails guard passed 75 fixture cases on the real lifted function; the loader and the page-side controllers ran in Node on both builds, and the panel script ran in headless Chromium against a local stand-in for the site whose worker models the bridge (it is not the game). Nothing was driven live. The 1.30× default comes from older logs of one track.

## 0.41.0 — best-opponent skill 9 for your AI car, panel fixes

- Skill: your racer keeps the game's player marker (254, read as −2) in its skill field, and the game's AI code clamps that marker to skill 0, the weakest level. Drag and Street X report their own waiting/applied state, and online sessions say "Off in online sessions · solo races only".
- Correction to the 0.40.0 note below: the game's global mode at 0x8650B0 makes normal skills read as 9 and keeps the player marker. It was never a way to give the player's car skill 9.
- Offline checks: 353 fixture cases on the real lifted wrapper (each site, each guard, online, other skills; everything except the returned skill is identical to 0.40.0), one real consumer (0x408430) through the game's own virtual dispatch, and the full patch chain, whose output 41470ae5… validates and compiles. Exact ed8d3359 only. Live racing is unverified.

## 0.40.0 — player-only catch-up in Drag and Street X

- Player-only constant catch-up now also runs in Drag and Street X (and forced Drag/Street X). Pace stays neutral (1.00×) there; only the catch-up strength applies. Drift stays excluded so drift scoring is unchanged.
- Native: inside the same 7 catch-up functions only, the Drag (0x89E7D8, 0x890108) and Street X (0x89E7E3, 0x89010C) exclusions now read as 0 (36 exact offsets, same-length edits). The identical check in the route-choice (shortcut) function is untouched, so shortcut policy stays off in Drag and Street X.
- If the game's drag driver is a different class from the road autopilot, the native publisher's ownership check still refuses it and the tools panel keeps showing "waiting"; nothing is forced.
- Never online. Exact ed8d3359 only. Offline: chain output b00036c5… validates and compiles. Live Drag/Street X racing is unverified.
- Not changed: your car's skill. The game maps the player's skill marker to 9 only in a special global mode; forcing it needs a reliable "AI owns the player car" signal inside the game code and was left out until 0.39/0.40 are tried in real races.

## 0.39.0 — player-only constant catch-up

- Race pace + catch-up now works with the game's Catch Up flag off and Mods: Rubberbanding set to Off or No boost. Before, its native publisher required Catch Up on and Rubberbanding = Original, so with those off your AI car never got any catch-up. New `godly-catchup.js` (exact ed8d3359 only, applied after the paced catch-up patch, pinned input/output hashes) makes those two checks pass in the 7 gated native functions (36 sites each, same-length edits). Opponents keep whatever the game setting gives them.
- With Rubberbanding off the game's own factor is 1, so your car gets a constant pace × strength handling/power factor for the whole race, whether it leads or trails. It never "waits" like game AI does when ahead.
- New defaults: paired race pace 1.00× (corner targets at the game's own speed, fewer wall hits) and catch-up strength 1.50× (a bit above the game's own skill-9 maximum of about +37–42%). Raise strength for more push; raising pace raises corner entry speed.
- Catch-up assistance is never enabled in online/LAN sessions, even with Allow network tools on.
- Drag, Drift and Street X are still excluded from paired catch-up. The JS readGain helper no longer checks the Catch Up flag or the (wrongly mapped on ed8) Rubberbanding host.
- Offline checks: the full extension patch chain reproduces the shipped 0.38.18 module exactly (92b567a3…), the new output (e40e7798…) validates and compiles. Live racing is unverified.

# NFSU2 Driving Tools: experimental v0.42.6

## 0.42.6 — direct worker loading and scoped 60946132 support

Adds the exact reviewed game build **60946132**. Its scoped native port covers the existing AI bridge, pace/corner hooks, rails, Drag handoff/protection, owned skill and paired catch-up. Online still requires the separate explicit permission. Stop, manual takeover, stale ownership and permission withdrawal retain their native guards.

The production page now supplies a verified compiled module through its existing game-worker startup observer. It leaves WebAssembly.compileStreaming unchanged. Per-worker message order, immediate port transfers, original shared-memory identity and primary/secondary worker consistency are checked offline. A timed-out, unsupported or failed preparation retains the original game module with tools disabled. Memory-port startup stays unverified and has no page memory tools.

The replacement is authorized by freshly read build metadata, an import/export interface check and complete source/output hashes. An opaque original compiled module cannot be hashed through this interface; matching its import/export names is an eligibility check, not proof of its bytes. Only the independently compiled replacement receives a verified tool profile.

On 60946132, **the tuner, leased forward geometry, per-target corner feedback, online car-category controls, race capture and destination travel are unavailable** pending their separate ports. Their implementations and previous build profiles remain included. The full 102c8d92 pipeline retains its exact prior output.

Current game guards, monitoring and report serialization are retained. A positive encoder result means serialization succeeded, including for reports containing observations. The offline checks do not establish multiplayer acceptance, account status or measured driving results.

The offline report check reproduced a selected-car-state observation from the actual NOS refill: one changed frame and observation flag 16 in controlled race and free-roam monitor contexts. Untouched baselines had zero changed frames and zero flags. The observed fields survived local encoding; no report was sent. This uses bounded native fixtures and synthetic session state, not a full game run. A different loader does not establish a report-free refill route.

The exact captured page check returned zero marks through updated startup and four fixture ticks; the frozen 0.42.5 startup produced API-wrapper mark 2. The fixture uses native-callable browser stand-ins, clean settings and default tool selections. Worker instance postMessage remains wrapped and is not selected by that captured check. Report markers and configuration remain unchanged. These page results do not cancel the separate native NOS observation.

Raw 60946132 SHA256: 81d2e32d7ee67bb93a8fafee4dbc17570f8d4980be238d7434e15c791904b945.
Scoped native output SHA256: 8efc4457e895e4992f56a0272f66718d3900901ff7fde95e760b7585fa6f9129.

## 0.42.5 — exact native corner-target feedback

Adds observed native target decisions to the road-race settings and diagnostics on verified game build **102c8d92**. A sample records the actual target before and after the existing corner-limit hook, requested/effective limit, decision outcome, guard reasons, ownership and sample age. These are **uncalibrated native target units**, not mph or m/s.

- The menu can distinguish a geometry reduction, cached reduction, an already-lower native target, a rejected/unresolved guard and a changed publication. This observes the existing driver; it does not change pace, braking, steering, grip, shortcuts or race outcomes.
- Receipts use the game's existing worker registration channel under the site's current security policy. The extension consumes its reserved messages before the game registry sees them. Current primary and secondary workers are bound to their module, memory and session.
- Stop/manual takeover, setting changes, ownership/permission loss, stale samples and route changes clear current evidence. Tick and command-sequence boundaries reject queued records from a previous activation. Existing historical race logs migrate without losing their prior columns.
- The optional observer must match its complete expected binary hash and compile before it receives a capability. Any failure keeps the previously compiled driving, online, tuner and forward-lease module.

Native parity, receiver, loader, page and diagnostic tests passed offline. The actual current worker also delivered a native receipt in isolated Chrome under its current CSP. This is not a live race or a measured driving improvement. Transport samples at most once per 1,000 guest ticks; it is not a lossless record of every setter call.

**Other work remains isolated:** the opponent Drag margin for tracks 4211–4213 passed controlled native tests but needs a proven production control connection; the default-off Drift bend-target experiment sometimes lowers native throttle or increases handbrake and needs a live comparison; destination routing passed controlled topology/GPS checks but has unresolved native queue/allocation, route-installation and parking issues. None of those experiments is activated by this package. A complete hosted travel → join → race → return loop remains unverified.

Saved profiles, stream HUD, radar, Clean View, tuner, Street X limits, Drag engine protection, explicit online permission and Stop/manual takeover keep their existing implementations. The preset tuner remains restricted to solo Performance Tuning; this release does not enable an ECU bypass.

Raw game SHA256: `2ba0b075721d80e75fc3fb9a3b0e4d2acae835d21fcc406d009669b83f81858d`.
Observed native output SHA256: `6005ed0fe49b641542e9e2909cf38d10108959f2d2ed2ac74144866281ad8cfc`.

## Previous release details

## 0.42.4 — clear rails and catch-up controls

This update fixes misleading assistance controls. It does not change the native driving, cornering, grip, power, shortcuts, tuning or network policy from 0.42.3.

- In a permitted rails road race or Street X, the assistance row says **Race pace · rails mode**. Catch-up strength is visibly inactive because paired grip/power assistance is not used there. Its selected value is retained for full physics and Drag.
- Switching rails off restores the strength control. Drag keeps its strength control and neutral paired pace. Recovery continues to show speed-only behavior, including when a stale physics sample still says rails is on.
- Messages, tooltips and accessible labels now distinguish pace targets from paired handling assistance. Online permission, Stop/manual takeover and saved driving preferences retain their existing behavior.

Validation: controlled page/mode regressions cover solo and online road races, Street X, Drag, recovery, permission changes, Stop and preserved settings. No live lap or measured grip/speed improvement is claimed. The existing nativeRoadTarget diagnostic is a sampled value in uncalibrated native units; it is not a per-setter explanation. A new per-setter receipt remains research and is not included.

The route-geometry and cache-lease changes from 0.42.3 remain unchanged. They still require the appropriate active AI, rails and Adaptive road-race speed settings for Circuit/Sprint/URL; live driving verification remains pending.

## 0.42.2 — race loop, preset tuner and mode corrections

Supports the verified game build **102c8d92**. Circuit, Sprint and Drag retain their existing driving requests and native paths. Saved profiles, streaming HUD layouts, Stop/manual takeover and explicit online permission are preserved.

- **Free roam:** current-build contact preview now recognizes cars eligible for the enabled no-clip categories, instead of unnecessarily reducing pace for them. The tuner requires the **solo Performance Tuning main screen**. Online tune writes and the separate ECU clamp-bypass recipe remain unavailable.

For tuning: enable the preset tuner, select the race preset in the game's solo Performance Tuning screen, Load settings, edit or Find tune, review Preview, then Stage selected preset. Use the game's Test Run to refresh driving physics and Save Profile to persist. Estimates are private native calculations, not measured lap times or confirmation of a disk save. Restore requires the same unchanged car, parts and preset.

The combined loader grants tuner capabilities only after both its native bridge and private evaluator compile. A failed optional tuner/city stage retains the last successfully compiled driving module. Current game metadata was rechecked before packaging. Unknown builds remain unsupported until independently verified.

Validation is offline: actual native snippets, private evaluator, controller/state-machine tests, actual-manifest compile/fallback tests and an isolated Chromium panel smoke check. No live race, live tuning session or complete hosted travel → JOIN → race → return was driven for this release. ## Previous update — new game build and "Stay on rails" (0.42.0)

nfsu2.xyz moved to game build **102c8d92**. 0.42.0 supports it: the whole reviewed native hook set from the previous build is applied to the new one as a single pinned transform (`native-transplant-102c.js`), and the page-side addresses for this build are in `102c-profile.js` and the build registry.

**Stay on rails** (Race / outrun tuning, on by default) is the cornering fix. The game drives opponents on a simplified physics mode and switches a car to full physics after a contact. For your AI-driven car that switch was permanent, and on full physics a raised pace overshoots corners. On rails your race AI car keeps the opponents' mode in solo Circuit, Sprint, URL and Street X.

- On rails, **Race pace + catch-up** only raises speed targets. The **Paired race pace** slider is the multiplier (default **1.30×**; Street X at most 1.15× unless Custom race pace is on). No power or grip boost is applied and Catch-up strength is not used. Drag keeps the paired boost.
- If the car stops for 3 seconds, the rails release so the game's normal physics can recover it, then return once it is moving again (two releases per race at most).
- Turn Stay on rails off to get the 0.41.0 behaviour back.
- This build is **solo/offline only**: Allow network tools is disabled and the online tools are unavailable. The preset tuner / dyno / ECU panel is not ported to this build.
- Offline checks only; nothing was driven live. The Driver line shows "on rails" while the car is on the simplified mode.

## Best-opponent skill for your AI car (0.41.0)

When the native AI drives your car, the game still reads the player's skill marker (254), and its AI code clamps that marker to skill 0, the weakest level. From 0.41.0 the AI's nitrous decisions, Drag launch delay and per-skill decision chances use **skill 9**, the best opponent level, while the extension's native AI owns your car in a solo session. Your racer record and save are not written. Opponents and online sessions are untouched. Where the game already treats the player's car better than any opponent (no random target-speed variance, no off-screen reset), it is left alone.

The Driver line shows "skill 9 …" while it applies. There is no switch: it follows the AI driver. Exact ed8d3359 only. Live racing is unverified. This release also makes the panel show the installed version (it stayed on 0.38.18) and removes a wrong "Game Catch Up is off · matching boost unavailable" line.

## Player-only constant catch-up (0.39.0)

**Race pace + catch-up** now gives your AI car a catch-up boost even when the game's Catch Up option is off and Mods: Rubberbanding is Off. Only your car is boosted; opponents keep the game setting. The boost is constant to the finish line (pace × strength), not gap-based, so it never eases off while leading.

Defaults: paired race pace **1.00×**, catch-up strength **1.50×**. Turn on Race-only automatic driver, open AI driver → Road-race settings, and make sure Race pace + catch-up is on. 0.40.0 adds Drag and Street X (catch-up strength only, pace neutral). Drift is not covered. Never applied online. Exact ed8d3359 only. Live racing is unverified.

## Retained full-physics publication correction

An active automatic driver could stay waiting for handling-input publication because the full-physics hook checked the runtime CPU structure against guest-object bounds. The runtime CPU lives outside that guest region. The v0.38.10 correction gives the CPU its own aligned, full-state check against actual Wasm memory size, while retaining the strict bounds and commitment checks for the car, physics objects and guest stack. The native physics calculation, selected pace and strength formulas remain unchanged.

The focused native regressions exercise the full publisher with a high runtime CPU address and no guest commitment bit for that CPU. Matching handling inputs remain required before extra paired pace is confirmed. A later live v0.38.10 export on 943ee537 recorded full four-tire and simplified combined-input publication with applied handling receipts. That verifies those observed publication paths; it does not establish improved cornering, race wins or complete .11 behavior. ## Handling evidence and selected city pace

Race pace + catch-up pairs a selected extra race pace P (1–2×) with an independent catch-up strength S (1–10×, quarter steps). Strength changes the assistance, not the speed target. The initial selections are pace2× and strength1×; these are authored controls, not a claim about the game's maximum. Loading follows an already selected Automatic/Race-only driver and does not acquire a manual car.

On exact AA/15e/943 builds, paired assistance follows the native physics path already selected by the game. Full physics uses four tire inputs; ordinary simplified AI physics uses its combined-grip input. This update corrects receiver identities and supports those paths separately without forcing a different physics mode. The native driver/car catch-up source caches remain unchanged. From original publication M, the handling scalar/aerodynamic divisor E is f32(f32(M×P)×S), and the nominal grip input is f32(E×P). Native modifiers remain in the combined-grip path. These are handling inputs, not measured engine power, tire grip, speed gains or a guarantee of winning.

Extra pace waits for current matching physical-input evidence. Full and simplified physics use different evidence kinds; requested pace, requested strength and verified application remain separate. The tools panel says requested pace while physical support is waiting. Bounded acknowledgement-rejection and native-stage codes enter the local log to distinguish failed identity/output checks from an unobserved publication. Owner, command, actual physical output, mode or permission changes revoke gain. Raised corner targets retain native use-time checks. When paired support is unavailable, the corner fallback uses the same neutral pace as the final target, avoiding an extra division by the selected pace. The base grade and braking tables remain planning assumptions, not load/contact measurements.

Online city clearance pacing keeps your explicitly selected free-roam factor as its ceiling, including values above 1×. Clear or unavailable observations retain that selection; an observed wall/vehicle hazard can reduce the runtime request and recovery moves back toward your ceiling. Unchanged observations no longer compound the same reduction on every page tick. A timing interruption preserves the current same-owner slowdown and selected ceiling without adding recovery credit. Selected corner-planning pace stays stable while the separate city request changes, so the reduction does not rebuild the native driver. Existing exact-build online detection, current ownership, mode and permission checks remain. These partial observations do not establish route safety or collision avoidance.

Free-roam corner assist now compensates its approach-braking input by pace squared on these same three builds, matching its existing corner-speed compensation. Previously the braking hook skipped ordinary free roam while its target still received the selected extra pace. Actual native getter/approach fixtures at 1/1.5/2/3× prove the corrected approach envelope retains the native braking assumption. Lower/equal pace, race commands and special modes retain their existing paths. Ownership, route, table, mode, permission and use-time checks remain. This fixes a calculation mismatch; it does not prove that it caused an individual crash or change steering, traffic avoidance or recovery.

The streaming HUD and race hub use factual English track names, including Outer Ring, Bayview Plaza and Airport Circuit Track 5, for all 100 primary race IDs. The city is labelled Bayview. Unknown locations display as unavailable instead of internal track numbers. These names are a static factual projection of the user's existing game language table; no game language asset is packaged, and no new live memory reader is needed. Widget positions, sizing and Clean View keep their existing behavior.

The viewer HUD shows MPH, gear, RPM, location, places driven, top speed and driving time. MPH follows the native HUD's float32 conversion and truncation; it is the game's display convention. The session meter starts with this page and includes both manual and automatic free-roam/race driving. It credits only consecutive live samples no more than 500 ms apart, so hidden tabs, menus and invalid observations cannot add an unobserved gap. Saved race-history totals never become session records. Rear radar keeps its nearest distance and dot labels in game-distance coordinates without claiming independent metre calibration. Technical driving status remains in the tools panel.

Rotate camera is a separate toggle, off on reload. It requires Camera bound to C and uses that key at a random interval from 45 to 120 seconds during active driving. Menus, text entry, photo/drone mode, unfocused/hidden pages and changed sessions rearm a fresh interval. Pressing C postpones the next change; F7/F9 switch rotation off and release any automatic key pulse while preserving a real held C key. A current worker error also disables it. The toggle changes no performance settings and requires no online driving-tool permission. Timer and page-input fixtures are distinct from live camera verification.

Stop, manual takeover and profile Load disable paired assistance. Saved profiles retain their schema and custom values. Independent power/grip controls are parked while paired assistance owns an ordinary road race or awaits restoration. Street X, Drag, Drift, Outrun and free roam retain their separate controls. A matching verified handling path, game Catch Up On / Original and explicit online permission are required. Unattended streaming autonomy remains unfinished.

On exact game builds aa2429fb, 15e5958f and 943ee537, selected pace now scales the native speed factor when the racing AI consumes it. It leaves the native driver cache and vehicle catch-up factor untouched. The previous wrapper could multiply its own cached result again before the game's next refresh; actual native fixtures reproduced 1.95 → 3.80 → 7.41. This correction removes that authored cache mutation. Native corner/behavior limits and the optional forward target can still lower the resulting target. Street X uses its existing native tables and corner controls; it receives the cache correction without the ordinary-road shortcut policy.

Adaptive road-race speed also enables a targeted experimental shortcut-choice policy on aa2429fb, 15e5958f and 943ee537. The car's raw player skill marker254/signed−2 stays intact. Only the eligible owned Race action's branch-choice check consumes skill9 instead. Native graph, category, probability, direction, event and checkpoint rules stay in control. It does not force every shortcut, replace pathfinding, or prove that a real shortcut completes correctly. Drag, Drift and Street X remain excluded from that branch policy. The 250 ms local driving trace retains separate requested/applied pace, current native driver and car catch-up factors, target/control values, corner-record coverage and planner evidence. The new factor readings are bounded read-only observations. Shortcut installed/requested flags are not branch-use receipts. Previous v0.38.5 trace rows survive a same-tab upgrade with nulls for the new fields. Samples, offline native tests and compiled output checks are distinct from live-game verification.

The preceding v0.38.7 native-calculated mode requested extra pace1 and observed original publication at Off/100. The later paired controls keep pace and strength separate. The traced Original catch-up calculation has no fixed numeric upper clamp; neither pace2× nor strength10× is a native game maximum. Driver/car source caches stay native.

This selection follows eligible Automatic/Race-only road racing by default unless the durable Stop marker is set; loading alone does not acquire a manually driven car. Switching it on arms Race-only AI if needed. The extension reports the native Catch Up flag and does not enable a global setting. There is no claim of perfect grip, automatic wins or live collision-free driving.

## Racing and cornering

- v0.38.7 removes a node-spacing error: inserting redundant straight nodes no longer changes the target for an identical physical bend. Curvature uses canonical bends with bounded physical arms; gradual arcs and accumulated75° priority turns remain included. The lower-only corner target retains priority over added pace and physical requests. These are planning assumptions, not a measured collision-free racing line.
- On AA/15e/943, corrects the authored continuous corner blend that could lower an already suitable native target. Command3 now leaves a tiny, nonlimiting bend at its native ceiling and uses a lower-only curvature target for limiting bends, with pace compensation. Only the authored command3 expression changes; free-roam/Street X corner commands, native branch selection and all publisher/physics paths retain their prior code. Offline native cases include unchanged gentle bends and a curvature-at-limit example improving its requested target from27.55 to38 at a native ceiling40; these are target values, not a live speed measurement.
- Calculated mode removes the stacked80%/15% corner discounts and75% braking assumption from its forward node plan: it uses the native grade-table values, no extra distance reserve and the minimum100ms reaction required by the existing target lease. The native corner-record hook retains its supported95% factor with zero sharp-turn discount and full native braking. Saved custom sliders remain available to explicit Adaptive mode when calculated mode is off. Native factors above4 pass through unchanged but exceed the existing node-adapter eligibility range; node-cap coverage is unavailable there, rather than clamping native catch-up to4.
- Ordinary-race Adaptive keeps your selected native pace when optional corner records are absent. The previous policy could hold a 2× selection at 1×, with repeated partial clearance scans reducing it to 0.75×. Those heading-ray observations remain diagnostic for races; native braking and existing corner controls continue.
- The optional forward planner no longer treats the end of a preview as a stopping obstacle or imposes a fixed straight-road ceiling. A straight or unsupported preview leaves native driving in control. Zero, negative and nonfinite optional caps cannot stop the native target.
- On exact **8abf9be8, 93cfc6e9, aa2429fb, 15e5958f and 943ee537**, node lookahead can use a game-thread receipt of the game's own grade-dependent grip and braking tables. It measures gradual and accumulated 75°+ bends on original checked road anchors, rather than creating extra curvature at interpolation knots. Its maximum horizon is 512 native route units, clipped to the actual checked source and the unchanged 24-anchor/40-node budgets; a short source stays short. A measured bend supplies a braking envelope; passing its anchor alone is not treated as proof of corner exit. The outgoing-heading release rule is authored assistance, not an unchanged native algorithm.
- Corrects two folded native evaluator guard cells in each d2fa4f4c, cd5b74d5 and 8abf9be8 forward adapter. They previously still addressed the older 3bdd9959 lookup. Only that authored slot helper changes in those earlier complete outputs; original native bodies and all other sections stay identical to v0.38.1. The new build uses independently verified current cells. Stale-cell fixtures now leave the older addresses empty.
- The native target lease binds the car, driver, route, request, event, clock, grade, ride/type table, selector, policy constants, committed pages and network permission. Changes revoke the optional target. Native lower, stop and reverse requests remain authoritative. Other supported forward builds retain read-only preview in the production page.
- Free-roam corner assistance now compensates for the selected pace. A 2× boost no longer doubles an assisted corner target. Previously ignored sampled gentle bends are checked when increased pace makes them limiting. Changing a boosted planning pace rebuilds the cached native route once; sub-native runtime changes share the original 1× plan. This still needs a usable native corner sample and does not prove that every free-roam turn is covered.
- Existing Street X corner formulas, Drag AI and engine protection remain. The AA pacing correction changes speed-factor composition without changing the native cache or adding a steering controller. No global skill-sentinel overwrite, lobby creation or opponent manipulation is included.

## Streaming display and rear radar

Shift+Insert hides controls, hub, launcher, Stop buttons, old Info HUD and the game's detailed performance column. Only selected Streaming HUD and rear radar remain. A second Shift+Insert restores the prior controls; F8 opens the menu. F7/manual and F9/Stop remain effective. Text-field paste is preserved.

The stats-only stream widgets and thin transparent rear half-circle have independent positions and 60–160% scales. Enable Edit HUD layout to move/resize them, then leave edit mode for click-through gameplay. Display layout is stored separately from driving profiles.

The radar's native blink-out flag is one byte. Reading four bytes could reject visible cars because neighboring native state was nonzero; both local and peer checks now read the byte. Solo and opted-in online fixtures cover this correction. The radar observes locally loaded cars behind you, shows the nearest eight within the selected 50–500 native-unit range, and retains ownership, commitment, list and freshness guards. It does not identify rivals or guarantee all online cars are loaded. Its live readings remain to be verified.

## Using the update

Keep the existing Desktop\NFSU2-Driving-Tools folder as the single unpacked extension location. Load this version into the existing extension, then refresh the game; a full Chrome restart was previously necessary to replace a retained older content script. Check the displayed version before testing.

For road races, use Automatic driver or Race-only automatic driver. Race pace + catch-up follows that driver by default on its supported builds, enabling the existing ordinary-race shortcut eligibility policy and corrected corner targets. Set pace and strength separately. Native probability, category, direction and checkpoint rules still decide whether a shortcut is taken; installed/requested flags are not evidence of taking one. Turn paired assistance off to use the custom Adaptive ceiling/corner sliders. For boosted free roam, enable Free-roam corner assist so its compensated native targets are requested. Online operation still requires Allow network tools. Stop remains available, and F9 works in Clean View.

The session-only City clearance pacing choice follows the explicit free-roam pace selection, from 0.75× to 3×, through initial acquisition and reacquisition. Current owned observations can lower its runtime request without changing that selection or its corner-planning ceiling. Unknown road coverage keeps the user-selected ceiling and never counts as route proof. It is not a steering or complete route-following system.

Saved profiles/schema, HUD/hub, online controls, car selection and the compact menu are retained. The R34 label identifies observed stock-name data; this update does not select or retune a car or claim a fastest R34. Race Hub reports bounded observed driving segments and native-speed samples, not fabricated finishes, wins or lap times.

## Retained v0.33 reference notes

## v0.33.0: Continuous adaptive corner targets

Adaptive road-race speed now has a separate native planning command. Every valid sampled nonzero bend receives a smooth curvature-based target, instead of requiring it to cross the older curvature threshold. Exact straights keep the requested target ceiling; existing native lower/stop results are never increased. The native distance-based braking calculation uses the same pace compensation.

The curve is deliberately conservative and experimental. It does not detect every corner on the map: the native planner may provide no corner records, skip a tail record, report zero curvature or use another route. It does not change steering, physical brakes, route lookahead, NOS or other cars. A hook hit is an observation of a past call, not proof the current corner is safe. Five fresh captures show hook hits despite reported missed turns, so the update is not presented as a proven fix for every failure.

Only adaptive road mode uses this new command. **Street X and existing free-roam/road-corner controls retain their exact prior behavior.** The new command also denies actual/forced Street X and known online Street X in its native guards. AI ownership, native handback, online permission, mode checks and watchdog remain required. This does not bypass an AI failure or acquire control automatically.

The option remains default-off/session-only and uses your current sliders without changing saved values. For the first comparison, try the existing defaults: 1.30× adaptive ceiling, 0.80 corner factor and 0.75 braking factor. Higher targets can still cause missed turns. The latest logs used 1.90×, 0.95 and 1.00 respectively; those settings were confirmed, not shown to be safe. Keep the working Street X setup unchanged.

Corner/braking hit counters now use the existing two-second telemetry sample cadence instead of replacing bounded history every quarter second. Discrete control/mode changes still log promptly. No raw route geometry, memory dump or additional personal data is collected.

Native tests execute the new corner and braking hooks against the pinned game routines, compare legacy commands byte-for-byte, and check protected outputs and guard denials. Live cornering, race results and browser rendering remain unverified. The final combined suite passes **1,942 tests, zero failures/skips/cancellations**. All four supported patched modules compile, with only the two reviewed corner/braking wrapper functions changed from v0.32.

It does not find, join, start, replay or vote for events.

The existing **Automatic driver** still includes free roam. Selecting either driver mode turns the other off. The race-only switch is **off by default**, stays armed between races on this page, and resets on page reload or profile Load. It is deliberately not added to saved profiles; existing saved choices and storage remain unchanged.

**F7, F9/Stop, or driving-key takeover during a race disarms race-only AI.** Manual steering in free roam leaves it armed. ## Optional adaptive road-race speed

A new **default-off, session-only** option coordinates the existing native route planner. Its separate straight-target ceiling defaults to **1.30×** and ranges from 1.00× to 2.00×. The native route uses distance to known corners to lower its target in advance while retaining a higher target on sufficiently long straights. This is a planned target factor, not a physical speed cap or a measured speed increase.

Enable either **Race-only automatic driver** or **Automatic driver**, then **Adaptive road-race speed** in AI driver → Road-race settings. Online use also requires **Allow network tools**. Adaptive mode uses the existing Race corner speed, Race sharp-turn margin and Race braking factor values, even when the separate Road-race hairpin assist switch is off. Lower braking factor requests earlier braking. It overrides the effective custom race pace only in eligible ordinary road races, without changing any saved switch or slider.

**Street X keeps the exact existing pace, corner and braking selections.** Adaptive mode is dormant in actual/forced Street X and the known online Street X mode. Drag, Drift/forced variants, Outrun and free roam are also excluded. Selecting adaptive mode does not turn on Automatic driver or network permission.

The optional ceiling stays constant while driving. The existing native route envelope varies by distance; JavaScript does not switch pace or reconstruct the driver at every corner. A deliberate setting or race-mode change may still require the existing OFF/acknowledgement/ON route reconstruction. Manual takeover, race end, permission withdrawal and the existing watchdog remain in force.

F7/manual driving keys stop AI and leave the optional selection dormant. F9/Stop, profile Load and page reload turn adaptive mode off. It is not added to saved tool profiles or legacy session preferences. Blur, hidden page and menus pause it normally. Turn it off to return to the prior controls after native handoff.

The HUD and local log distinguish a request, matching native pace acknowledgement, and observed corner/braking hook evidence. These counters do not measure braking success, safe corner entry or a clean lap. There is no new steering, obstacle avoidance, NOS control, added route horizon, opponent manipulation or collision protection. Higher targets can still cause crashes. Start at 1.30× and assess one change at a time.

The original v0.32 option used page orchestration only. The v0.33 continuous-corner update changes the two native planner wrappers and teaches the controller a separate adaptive command. Existing planner commands retain their prior behavior; engine tuning, NOS, Drag-retention, tuner and saved-profile implementations are untouched. Exact-native synthetic tests support the route-speed envelope; live racing, lap times, wins and browser layout remain unverified.

## Retained v0.25.0: Saved extension settings profiles

**Saved tool profiles** saves named groups of extension settings in this browser for this game site. Save your current choices, then load them together instead of enabling each tool separately. ## Retained v0.24.0: Opted-in online Drag engine blowout protection

For **online or LAN Drag**, enable both **Drag racing → Disable Drag engine blowouts** and **Online / LAN opt-in → Allow network tools** before the engine blows. Solo Drag needs only the blowout toggle. Exact **93af6ccb** and **78e2bb69** builds are supported. The heat toggle works independently of Automatic driver and Manual drag assist. It starts off for a fresh tab, remembers your choice in the same tab, and F9 clears it. Network permission starts off after reload and F9.

Only the current linked local player's engine is eligible, during active Drag with full physics. Opponent, stale, unowned, invalid and already-blown engines remain excluded. This is local protection, not a change to remote engines, network packets or server rules. Follow server rules; online changes can trigger integrity checks or sanctions.

Enable it **before** the engine blows. It does not repair an already-blown engine or reverse a lost race. While enabled it supplies the game's own disabled-heat sentinel, intentionally discarding accumulated heat. Turning it off resumes normal heating from zero after the next native full-physics setup. It does not change shifts, throttle, steering, pace, power, torque, limiter, NOS decisions or opponents, and does not trigger an AI restart.

The exact native heat routine and its original instructions remain intact. An authored prefix checks active Drag, current player/car/race/engine identity, full physics, finite unblown heat, permission epoch and heartbeat before changing only the current engine's heat field. Online/LAN additionally requires literal network permission. Added diagnostics show bounded heat/blown/limit observations and the requested toggle.

Controlled native tests cover 600 online over-redline updates on each supported module, low and high runtime CPU addresses, opt-out restoring native heating and rejected ownership/stale states. No successful live Drag race, HUD appearance or win is claimed. Repeated native NOS cycling is unchanged.

This stays combined with the complete preset tuner, opted-in online corner/braking settings and local online race-car filtering. Solo/Street X driving formulas remain unchanged. No Lap Knockout experiment or unverified native grip/downforce multiplier is enabled.
